text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: [ALERT] Service: inference-api-prod - elevated 5xx rates from us-west-2 region (detected 03:02 UTC). Auto-escalation -> #incidents. See metrics: https://console.metrics.example/region/us-west-2/alerts/3194005678 :rotating_light:

infra-oncall: Ack. I'm on call. Pulling logs and LB metrics now.

sre-alex: seeing ELB 503/504 spikes and concurrent connection resets. Target health shows intermittent UNHEALTHY in us-west-2b. EBS latency elevated on a subset of instances.

sre-june: +1. ENI detach events in us-west-2b around 03:00 UTC correlating with spikes. Could be a noisy host or AWS networking flapping in that AZ.

netops-ryan: AWS Health dashboard shows a partial networking impairment in us-west-2b: https://status.aws.amazon.com/incident/XYZ-123 (reported). AWS ticket created (xxxx-aws-5678).

support-ops: customer-impact estimate: roughly 7% p95 latency increase global; 23 tenants reporting errors in last 20 minutes (mostly in us-west customers). Flagging top 5 paying customers now.

infra-oncall: immediate mitigation options: 1) Shift Route53 weights to reduce traffic to us-west-2b AZ variant (if we have AZ-aware records), 2) disable AZ for ELB target groups so traffic drains away from affected instances, 3) scale up healthy AZs and enable cross-zone balancing. Thoughts?

sre-alex: I can run an ELB AZ disable and start draining targets in 2-3m. Will also remove problem instances from auto-scaling groups to prevent immediate replacements into the bad AZ.

sre-june: I'll prepare the Route53 change. Suggest shift 80% weight to us-west-2a and 20% to other regions if cross-region failover is allowed.

netops-ryan: Before Route53 weight change - confirm DNS TTLs. Our records have 60s TTL for the public edge records. Quick change will propagate fast enough for client retries.

pm-elis: Notify ENG-PLATFORM and Sales about customer-facing impact. I'll draft a short note for the status page and add affected customer list.

support-ops: posting incident banner now: "We are investigating elevated errors for customers in us-west-2. We will post updates every 15 minutes."

sre-alex: executing ELB drain now. Command (running):
``` 
# drain targets in us-west-2b
aws elbv2 set-subnets --load-balancer-arn $LB_ARN --subnets subnet-az-a subnets-subnet-az-c
# disable AZ handlers via console as fallback
```

sre-june: Route53 change ready. Planned weights: us-west-2a=80, us-west-2b=0, us-east-1=15, eu-west-1=5. Applying now.

netops-ryan: Confirmed route53 weights updated. Monitoring for client reconnections and error rate slope.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Action logged: ELB drain + Route53 weight shift. Incident severity: SEV2. Pager escalation updated.

infra-oncall: Observing traffic shift. 5xx rate trending down in us-west overall. Some stuck sessions still hitting unhealthy instances - ELB draining should handle those within deregistration delay (300s).

support-ops: Customer reports: 3 of top 5 reported resolved after ~6 minutes. Keeping the banner live.

sre-alex: AWS confirmed they saw high ENI detach noise in us-west-2b and are investigating host-level networking. They've advised not to relaunch into the affected subnets. Opening a Capacity hold for us-west-2b in our autoscaling policies.

sre-june: Can we put a temporary AZ routing policy in the console to avoid scheduling new instances into 2b? Setting ASG subnets to exclude 2b now.

infra-oncall: Done. ASG subnets updated, no new instances will be launched into 2b until we clear.

netops-ryan: Longer-term mitigation: consider pre-warming cross-region failover for specific customers and reduce DNS TTLs further during incidents. We'll add to postmortem action items.

pm-elis: Agree. I'll own the postmortem and coordinate customer comms and RCA timeline.

customer-success: Looping in account teams for the few affected customers. Sharing immediate mitigation steps and ETA for next update (~15m).

support-ops: Banner update: "We have rerouted traffic away from the impacted AZ; errors have decreased. AWS is investigating. We will continue to monitor."

sre-alex: Monitoring stack traces - a small fraction of retries still hitting 504 due to long-lived connections to problem instances. Plan: reduce ELB deregistration delay for the pool to 60s to speed up drain, then re-enable once healthy. Will do in 2m.

infra-oncall: Proceed with decreasing deregistration delay for this LB only. Command (applied):
``` 
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn $TG_ARN --attributes Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=60
```

sre-june: After change, 5xxs dropped to baseline. Confirming with metrics and Synthetics.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Mitigation successful. Recovery mode entered. Please start collecting timeline and artifacts for postmortem.

netops-ryan: AWS updated status: "Networking issue impacting subset of instances in us-west-2b" - root-cause under investigation. They estimate next status update in ~90 minutes.

infra-oncall: Handoff: I'm going offline soon. Handoff to @sre-june for the rest of the incident. Full context in this thread.

sre-june: Taking lead. I'll keep monitoring and coordinate with AWS contact.

pm-elis: Noted. I'll schedule a post-incident review for tomorrow. Actionables so far: 1) Add automated ASG subnet exclusions on AWS incident signals, 2) Lower DNS TTL during incidents, 3) Improve detection of ENI detach correlation with LB health, 4) Customer comms templating.

support-ops: Final banner: "Traffic successfully rerouted, functionality restored for impacted customers. We continue to monitor and expect gradual recovery of the affected AZ. No further customer action required at this time." :wave:

customer-success: Passing closure note to account teams.

incident-bot: :memo: Incident logged as 3194005678. Please ensure postmortem filed in #postmortems and tag SEV2.

sre-june: Closing this thread for active mitigation. Will update once AWS provides RCA and we have postmortem draft. Thanks all for quick turnaround. :white_check_mark:
